result.title: Training Mixed-Monotone Neural Networks for Verification Without Set Propagation
result.summary: Most formal verification approaches for neural networks conservatively enclose the output set of the neural network. However, computing a tight output enclosure is in general computationally hard. We sidestep this challenge with a novel neural network architecture that realizes mixed-monotone functions as the difference of monotone subnetworks. By utilizing the theory on mixed-monotone systems, this reduces the computation of a tight output enclosure from complicated set propagation to two simple forward passes of opposite corners of an input interval. Moreover, because the size of the resulting enclosure is a closed-form function of the weights of the neural network, we can directly minimize it during training. We prove a lower bound on the size of any such enclosure, given by the total variation of the represented function generalized to several inputs, which makes it possible to compare the tightness of the enclosure against the optimum. Our evaluation on regression and dynamical-system benchmarks demonstrates that our training reduces the enclosure size to within 0.5% of the lower bound without sacrificing prediction accuracy. Computing our enclosure is orders of magnitude faster than CROWN and $α$-CROWN and on deep networks it is also tighter than zonotope propagation and CROWN, while its size exceeds that of $α$-CROWN by only 5.1%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出以「两个单调子网络之差」实现混合单调函数的网络架构，使输出包络可由区间两端的两次前向传播直接得到，并在训练中闭式最小化包络大小，同时给出基于总变差的下界用于评估紧致度。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作虽面向形式验证，但其「用一次前向得到状态集合紧致界、并将界的大小纳入训练目标」的思路，可能为 latent 推理状态的不确定性刻画与低成本验证、以及计算预算与紧致度的权衡提供可核查的启发。
